label: prop:baryon-octet-decomposition
title: The baryon octet and the degeneracy of its weight diagram
html:
Proposition. The baryon octet and the degeneracy of its weight diagram

The mixed channel \lambda = (2,1) of V^{\otimes 3} carries the baryon octet. Unlike the decuplet, its weight diagram is degenerate --- and that degeneracy is the one piece of eightfold-way structure in this chapter which constrains rather than describes.

Conditional on N = 3 (Proposition), the three-fold product decomposes as

  \mathbf{3} \otimes \mathbf{3} \otimes \mathbf{3}
  \;=\;
  \mathbf{10} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1},
  \qquad
  27 = 10 \cdot 1 + 8 \cdot 2 + 1 \cdot 1 .

The two octets are one flavour irrep counted with the multiplicity \dim S^{(2,1)} = 2 of its Hecke partner, not two different multiplets. The decuplet is treated in the preceding proposition; the octet is the subject here.

The eight states

Writing the weight as (2I_3, Y) keeps every entry an integer.

State Content 2I_3 Y I
\mathfrak{p} uud +1 +1 1/2
\mathfrak{n} udd -1 +1 1/2
\Sigma^{+} uus +2 0 1
\Sigma^{0} uds 0 0 1
\Lambda uds 0 0 0
\Sigma^{-} dds -2 0 1
\Xi^{0} uss +1 -1 1/2
\Xi^{-} dss -1 -1 1/2

\Sigma^0 and \Lambda share both the quark content uds and the weight (0,0). They are separated only by isospin, I = 1 against I = 0. The octet's eight states therefore occupy seven lattice points: six on the hexagon and two stacked at the centre.

The degeneracy is a constraint

Every other eightfold relation this chapter examines --- Gell-Mann--Okubo, the decuplet equal-spacing rule and Coleman--Glashow --- turns out to be an identity of its first-order ansatz, true for all parameter values and therefore evidence for no mechanism. This one is different, and the difference is machine-checked sorry-free in QOU/Eightfold/OctetWeightDegeneracy.lean:

  • The decuplet's ten weights are pairwise distinct (decuplet_weights_nodup); the octet's eight are not (octet_weights_not_nodup), with exactly one collision, at the origin (lambda_sigma0_same_weight, octet_degeneracy_only_at_origin).
  • Hence no function of the weight alone can separate \Lambda from \Sigma^0. The statement holds for an arbitrary target, not for real-valued masses alone (weight_function_cannot_separate_lambda_sigma0). Any mass formula built from (2I_3, Y) predicts \mathfrak{m}_\Lambda = \mathfrak{m}_{\Sigma^0}.

Experiment gives \mathfrak{m}_\Lambda \approx 1115.7 MeV against \mathfrak{m}_{\Sigma^0} \approx 1192.6 MeV --- a 77 MeV gap, about 7\%, two orders of magnitude larger than the 0.8\% Coleman--Glashow residual. The class is excluded outright.

This is a scope-(b) structural exclusion, and the invariant justifying it is proved rather than asserted: non-injectivity of the weight map on the octet. The obligation it creates falls on every framework, this one included --- a label beyond (2I_3, Y) must be supplied. Physically that label is isospin, which is demonstrably not a function of the weight (isospin_not_a_function_of_weight). The decuplet incurs no such obligation (decuplet_weight_function_separates), which is precisely why its equal-spacing rule runs on Y alone while Gell-Mann--Okubo needs the isospin Casimir as well.

Two twos, kept apart

The multiplicity \dim S^{(2,1)} = 2 and the \Lambda/\Sigma^0 degeneracy are both doublings, and they are unrelated. The first counts copies of the whole eight-dimensional irrep inside V^{\otimes 3}; the second counts states over a single lattice point inside one copy. Reading either as the other would make the octet's extra label look as though the Hecke algebra already supplied it. It does not: the channel arithmetic (schur_weyl_cube_arithmetic) and the degeneracy count (octet_deficit_is_one) are recorded separately for that reason.

What the framework supplies

The decomposition above, and everything drawn from it, is conditional on N = 3. The framework's single-fibre construction gives \dim V = 2, at which the Schur--Weyl row cap removes the singlet entirely and there is no octet to carry a weight diagram --- a proved obstruction, not an approximation (Proposition). No construction here supplies N = 3.

Nothing on this page is fitted and nothing is wired to any computation; the PDG masses are comparators. What the framework does contribute is the negative result: a weight-only mass formula for the octet is structurally impossible rather than inaccurate, so any future derivation must carry the isospin label from the start.
